topics.title: The NPD Stage Framework: Annual Mood Board to Four-Month SKU Board

steps.text: NPD Framework Aligned with AOP Goals

The Annual Mood Board is a yearly planning framework. Begins with generating 50-100 product ideas based on solid research. These ideas are developed by first identifying categories and then finalizing them at the SKU level. This process helps define the company’s category direction for the year, aligning with its growth strategy and overall vision. Ideas are screened and evaluated through detailed market research based on: Market demand Sales potential Competition Pricing & Margins Seasonality Approved products are allocated across Q1–Q4. Products are categorized into: Core Sub-categories Innovation Trend-driven segments SKU-level planning is developed for the first eight months, including forecasting. Followed by tracking, execution, and continuous performance monitoring. Ensures structured and data-driven product launches throughout the year.
Four Month SKU Board (TAT should be added in all tasks)

Category Direction Review - Things to check: Growth categories (Plants, Gardening kits, Home decor, etc.) Seasonal opportunities Market trends Sales performance of existing SKUs Outcome: Identify which categories should grow, sustain, or reduce focus. 2. Product Idea Pool From the Annual Mood Board / Idea Bank, shortlist ideas for each category. Outcome: Create a list of potential SKUs per category. 3. Commercial Feasibility Check Evaluate each shortlisted product on: Costing feasibility Vendor availability Packaging requirement MOQ constraints Margin expectations Outcome: Filter out non-feasible ideas. 4. Demand & Sales Alignment Discuss with sales / marketplace / marketing teams. Questions to answer: Which SKUs are required by marketplaces? What price range works best? Any upcoming campaigns or seasonal demand? Outcome: Prioritize high-demand products.

RM purchase planning Calculate final demand using below logic Demand = SOH + All open POs - all months projected consumption - buffer
